answer_text:
Assume the curve is one arch of the cycloid, i.e. \(t\) runs from \(0\) to \(2\pi\).

Given

\[
x=a(t-\sin t),\qquad y=a(1-\cos t),
\]

we have

\[
dx=a(1-\cos t)\,dt,\qquad dy=a\sin t\,dt.
\]

Then

\[
x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a(t-\sin t)\cdot a\sin t\,dt
-
a(1-\cos t)\cdot a(1-\cos t)\,dt.
\]

So

\[
x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a^2\left[(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2\right]dt.
\]

Simplify the bracket:

\[
(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2
=
t\sin t-\sin^2 t-1+2\cos t-\cos^2 t
\]

\[
=
t\sin t-(\sin^2 t+\cos^2 t)-1+2\cos t
\]

\[
=
t\sin t-2+2\cos t.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\int x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a^2\int_0^{2\pi}\left(t\sin t-2+2\cos t\right)dt.
\]

Now compute each part:

\[
\int_0^{2\pi} t\sin t\,dt
=
\left[-t\cos t+\sin t\right]_0^{2\pi}
=
-2\pi,
\]

\[
\int_0^{2\pi} -2\,dt=-4\pi,
\]

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}2\cos t\,dt=0.
\]

Thus,

\[
\int x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a^2(-2\pi-4\pi)
=
-6\pi a^2.
\]

The negative sign corresponds to the orientation induced by increasing \(t\) over the cycloid arch. Hence,

\[
\boxed{-6\pi a^2}
\]
